chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man goes out on his journey and passes by a village belonging to him or a house, then stays in it. He said: he should complete the salat (prayer), even if he does not have in it except a single palm tree, and he should not shorten; and let him observe sawm (fasting) if the fast comes upon him while he is in it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What these reports contain of the command to perform fully in a person’s estate admits of several possibilities. Among them is that full prayer only becomes binding on him when he resolves to stay for ten days, and that which indicates this is what...

key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs in full, without shortening

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler complete salat (prayer) and observe sawm (fasting) when staying in his own property or village?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of a traveler who passes through or stays in a property or village that belongs to him. It states that he performs the salat (prayer) in full and fasts there, while the compiler then notes that these reports may be understood as applying when he intends to reside for ten days.
